newsitem.title: USA: Group sees Pacific economies in Americas stable.
newsitem.headline: Group sees Pacific economies in Americas stable.

text.p: Economic growth in the Pacific countries of North and South America will continue at close to the present pace for the most part, the Pacific Economic Cooperation Council (PECC) said on Tuesday.

In its 1997/1998 annual report, the PECC, a research group, forecast acceleration of growth in Canada and Colombia, a moderate slowdown of Chile's rapid expansion and little change in the pace of growth in the United States, Peru and Mexico.
Canadian Gross Domestic Product is forecast to grow 2.9 percent this year and 2.7 percent in 1998 after growing 1.5 percent last year, the PECC said.
"Canada's persistent large output gap continues to argue for generally stimulative monetary policy, even in the presence of higher U.S. interest rates," the report said.
Canadian consumer price increases are expected to pick up slightly to 2.2 percent this year and 2.3 percent next year from 1.6 percent in 1996, it said.
Growth in the United States is expected to jump to 3.2 percent this year from 2.4 percent last year, before falling back to 2.3 percent in 1998, it said.
The PECC said it expected U.S. Federal Reserve policymakers to hike short-term interest rates by another 25-50 basis points beyond its 25-basis point hike of March 25.
The report foresaw no improvement in the U.S. current account imbalance. It said consumer price increases should slow down to 2.3 percent in 1996 and 2.1 percent this year from 2.9 percent in 1996.
In Mexico, the PECC said further progress in the country's return to economic growth can be achieved only through the control of inflation, so that real wages can rise and interest rates can decline.

Mexican GDP is seen moving sideways this year to 5.0 percent from 5.1 percent in 1996, before ticking up to 5.5 percent in 1998. On the inflation front, consumer price increases are seen dropping to 17.9 percent this year and 11.9 percent next year from 27.7 percent in 1996.

Peru's GDP is expected to grow 3.0 percent this year from 2.8 pecent in 1996 before slipping to 2.4 next year, assuming the government maintains tight fiscal and monetary policies aimed at discouraging private consumption, it said. Consumer price increases are expected to drop to 9.1 percent this year and 9.6 percent next year from 11.8 percent in 1996.
After a sharp downturn in which government tightening slowed Colombia's GDP growth to 2.1 percent in 1996, growth is expected to rebound to 4.0 percent this year and 5.0 percent next year, the PECC.
The PECC said it expects consumer price increases of 19.0 percent this year and 20.0 percent next year after 21.6 percent last year, the PECC said.
Chile's vibrant economy is expected to slow to 5.6 percent this year from 7.2 percent last year before returning to a rate closer to its potential of 6.3 percent in 1998, the PECC said.
Consumer price increases in Chile are forecast to trend down to 5.5 percent this year and 4.5 percent next year from 6.6 percent in 1996, it said.
